title: What makes a good band: rehearsal and love of jazz
summary: Wiggs wants a well rehearsed band and says no white jazz musician in New Orleans loves jazz enough to play for fun.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Big band discipline versus small-group freedom

blocks.x: I'm afraid so. Well, let's see. Is there anything else about the New Orleans jazz?
Anything else about the New Orleans style of playing or anything about organizing bands or the way you like... What do you think is a good band?
I mean, the right style to play

I like a band to be rehearsed. You can still get that good new audience sound with a band that knows what it's doing. I just don't like to play like they play down here. Now, when I say down here, I've only been living here for 63 years, you see, since the day I was born, except when I left town for a few years. But I don't like the way they play down here. Unless I was playing with a good Negro rhythm section, you see, then you can do no wrong. But here, where you're walking on a tightrope with a rhythm section that's going to upset you any two seconds, I want a band well rehearsed. And you can't get them well rehearsed. Not only that, you can't get anybody in New Orleans... Really, nobody in New Orleans loves jazz. That's the whole truth of it. I mean, no... I say nobody. I mean no white jazz musicians like jazz. Because if they like jazz, they'd like to get together and play. But one of them has this reason for not playing. I only play when I get paid. The other can't play because somebody brings his babies over to their house. And another one can't play because he's always got jobs. And another one can't play because he's got to deliver babies all the time. And there's always a reason. Now, all over the country, you can get rarities such as string instruments that will be delighted to get together and play once a week. Think of Mencken's group and your group to get together on strings. All over the country, you find people that love music enough so that they want to get together once a week. For 17 years, I've been trying to get a group together that would play once a week just for the love of jazz. So I finally gave up last year. It just is not possible. So my conclusion is that nobody, no white man that can play jazz in this town really loves it. Because if he loved it, he'd love to play it.
